Nambiandar Nambigal has sung about this place in Thiruthondar Thiruvandhadhi, and Sekkizhar Peruman has sung about it in Periya Puranam. This is the *Sthala Puranam* of Thiruppanandal. Now, in the time of Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar, the Lord's *Lingam*, which had bent for the woman named Thadagai, remained in that leaning state. The Chola king was trying to straighten that leaning *Lingam*. Hearing this, our Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar set out from Thirukadavur and reached this sacred place called Thiruppanandal. We will continue to contemplate. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 162, Ilaimalindha Sarukkam, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar Puranam. In the sacred place of Thiruppanandal, once upon a time, for a woman named Thadagai, the Lord bent His *Shivalingam*. When Thadagai came to worship and offer a garland to the Lord, by the Lord's divine play, Thadagai's upper garment slipped. Holding her upper garment with both hands, she prayed to the Lord that He should accept the flower garland in her hands. Therefore, the Lord then bent His *Shivalingam* and graciously allowed the woman named Thadagai to offer the garland to Him. That bent *Lingam* remained in its bent state. Now, until the time of Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar, that *Shivalingam* remained bent. Similarly, in countless sacred places, when the Lord manifested His divine grace, we can still see Him enshrined with those very signs. In Perur, near Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu, there are hoof marks of a calf of Kamadhenu (divine cow) on the Lord's *Shivalingam*. In Thirumullaivayil, the cut mark from a sword is on the Lord's *Lingam*. In Kanchipuram, when the Goddess was worshipping a *Shivalingam* and the Lord caused the Kampa River to flood, the Mother embraced the *Shivalingam*. At that time, the marks of the Mother's bangles and breasts were imprinted on the *Shivalingam*. Even today, the Lord appears in Kanchipuram with those marks of the Mother's bangles and breasts. Thus, in many places, the Lord still appears with the signs of His divine grace. Similarly, here in Thiruppanandal, for the woman named Thadagai, He stood in a leaning form, and even now, He appears as a leaning *Lingam*. This was the case until the time of Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar; the Lord remained there as a leaning *Lingam*. The king of that country, seeing the Lord's *Shivalingam* leaning, was saddened and greatly desired to straighten it and worship it. Generally, the Lord remains in those sacred places with those signs so that everyone can witness His divine grace. This is because devotees who come later should see those signs on the *Shivalingam*, remember the Lord's divine plays and gracious deeds, and thereby their devotion to the Lord should grow. The Lord appears in those forms to bestow grace upon beings. It is an *Agamic* (scriptural) rule that these signs should be seen and worshipped as they are. Here too, the king should have worshipped the leaning *Lingam* as he saw it. It is wrong to think of repairing the *Lingam* as if it were a damaged temple or other structure. That is, if a part of a temple is damaged, it is repaired. But it is wrong to think of repairing the leaning *Lingam* in the same way. Even today, some people, transgressing the rules, displace, elevate, transform, and repair the Lord's idols in various ways as they wish. This is a great mistake. According to *Agamic* rules, all temples should be worshipped as the Lord's form appears. We should not elevate, lower, repair, or transform the Lord's *Lingam* or other idols as we wish. This is a great mistake. Even in temples, only damaged parts should be repaired, and they should be restored to their original state before the damage occurred. This is the rule. Thirumoola Deva Nayanar's Thirumandiram, in the second *Thanthiram* (chapter), 19th section, contains verses under the title "Thirukkoil Kutram" (Faults in Temples). It condemns faults that occur in temples. The first verse states: "If a fixed *Lingam* is removed and installed elsewhere, before it is done, the king's rule will be destroyed. Before he dies, a great disease will afflict him. Our leader Nandi has declared this." It means that if an immovable *Shivalingam* in a temple is removed and installed in another temple or another place, before that act is completed, the king's rule will collapse. The one who committed this crime will suffer from leprosy before his death and die in great pain. Thirumoolar says that our leader Nandi Peruman has firmly declared this to us. But here in Thiruppanandal, the Lord remains as a leaning *Lingam* so that everyone can realize His divine grace. The king, out of love, desired to straighten that leaning *Lingam* and worship it. Although the king undertook this action out of love and devotion to the Lord, we should keep in mind that this is also love that transgresses the rules. But the king, having great devotion and enthusiasm for Lord Shiva, tried to straighten the Lord's *Lingam*. He used his elephant armies and other armies, commanding them to try and straighten the *Shivalingam*. He made great efforts. Although the king acted out of love and enthusiasm, the Lord remained without straightening His form. This is the implication here. The king tried to straighten the *Shivalingam* using the strongest elephants in his elephant armies. Here, the king greatly valued the strength of his elephant armies, but he did not consider the strength of the Lord who gave them strength. He did not attempt it with a humble mind, considering the Lord's immense strength and power. Therefore, the Lord did not stand straight. His efforts did not yield results. But in the Nayanar's story, when the Nayanar tied a rope around his neck, the Lord stood straight. The Lord, who was unattainable to Brahma and Vishnu, who searched for His feet and head with their body and soul, later appeared and blessed them when they realized their powerlessness and praised Him. Similarly, the king tried to straighten the Lord with his strength, the strength of his armies, and the strength of his elephant armies. But the Lord did not allow it. But when the Nayanar, risking his life for the Lord, tied a rope around his neck and tried to straighten the Lord, the Lord straightened Himself. The Lord yielded to the Nayanar's boundless love and stood straight. This is the story we are about to see. Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar heard about the king's attempts to straighten the leaning *Lingam*. He understood that the king was doing this out of great love and desire for the Lord. Hearing this, the Nayanar set out from Thirukadavur to worship the Lord enshrined in Thiruppanandal. On the way, he visited all the other sacred places and reached Thiruppanandal. Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar, who set out from Thirukadavur, first visited the Lord of Thirukadavur, then came to the sacred place of Thiruakkur and visited Thanthondrinathar, then visited Suvarnapureeswarar in Semponnar Koil, then came to Mayavaram, Thirumayiladuthurai, and visited Mayuranathar, then came to the sacred place of Thiruthuruthi and visited Uttharavedheeswarar, then came to Thiruvavaduthurai and visited Masilamani Eeswarar, then came to Aduthurai and worshipped the Lord, then came to Thirumangalakudi and worshipped Pranavaratheeswarar. Thus, he visited all the sacred places on the way from Thirukadavur to Thiruppanandal and reached Thiruppanandal. It is a rule of pilgrimage that those who travel from one sacred place to another should visit all the places on the way before reaching and visiting the intended destination. We read in the Puranam of Thaduthadkonda that when Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worshipped in Thiruthuraiyur, he desired to worship Nataraja Peruman in Chidambaram. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, who intended to go to Chidambaram, visited Thiruvadhigai Veeram, Thirumanikkuzhi, Theerthanagiri, and other places on the way. Similarly, here, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar set out from Thirukadavur, visited all the sacred places on the way, and reached Thiruppanandal. Those who attempt to travel from one sacred place to another should worship the places on the way. Even if the sacred places on the way have been worshipped before, they should be worshipped again. This rule is stated in Periya Puranam. It is a rule shown by our *Samayacharyas*. Therefore, the practice of going directly from one place to another and visiting only that place, which we follow now, is improper. This is what we learn from this. Thus, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar reached Thiruppanandal. He reached Thiruppanandal, a land where Vedic scholars live, who nurture and maintain the three fires so that the Vedic path does not weaken. He saw the elephants and armies, engaged in the service of straightening the *Shivalingam* in that temple, exhausted and suffering from their hard work. Therefore, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar thought that he too should share in their suffering. Here, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar did not try, saying, "I will also join them and make the *Shivalingam* stand straight." He did not try, saying, "Like the elephants and armies, I will also use my strength to make the Lord stand straight." Because it would be foolish to try to do something that powerful elephants and soldiers could not do with his own strength. It is not the act of a wise person. If he were to think, "I will make the *Shivalingam* stand straight," it would be an attempt born of arrogance. Moreover, as we have already seen, it would be contrary to the *Shiva Dharma*. Therefore, here, the Nayanar thought that this was impossible for him. But now, what the Nayanar thought was, "Let us share in the suffering and exhaustion of those elephant armies, and try to reduce their suffering." This was the Nayanar's thought here. The Nayanar thought that he too should share in the suffering of the elephants and armies. The Nayanar is now trying only with the thought that if he shares even a little in their suffering, their suffering will be reduced a little. He came to Thiruppanandal to see the king, having heard that the king was making such efforts out of love for the Lord. Reducing the suffering of the elephants and armies who are engaged in this loving service of the king and suffering there is also the duty and righteousness of devotees. It is also the duty and righteousness of Shiva devotees. Therefore, the Nayanar tried. Even in worldly life, we see that when people who share the same love share in each other's suffering, that suffering is reduced, and when they share their joy with others, that joy increases. Similarly, here, the Nayanar began to try with the thought that if he shared in the suffering of those creatures, elephants, and soldiers who were engaged in the Lord's service and were exhausted and suffering, their suffering would be reduced a little. The Nayanar took a strong rope. He threaded flowers on one end of it. He made it into a loop and placed it on the *Shivalingam*. Because the rope the Nayanar took was very strong, if he placed it directly on the *Shivalingam*, the rope would hit the *Shivalingam* and cause harm to the Lord. Therefore, to prevent harm to the Lord, he wrapped the rope with flower garlands and silk cloths, and then placed it on the *Shivalingam*. But he made a loop on the other strong end of the rope and put it around his neck. Now, one part wrapped with flowers was on the Lord's *Shivalingam*, and the other part of the strong rope with knots was around the Nayanar's neck. Now, the Nayanar worshipped and praised the Lord, and began to pull the rope that was around his neck. In accordance with the saying, "Meditate with a unified mind," the Nayanar's mind was unified with the Lord, and the rope was like a rope twisted with threads of love. "Plant the staff of relationship and churn with the rope of awareness, and He will stand before you," says Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal's Thevaram. The Nayanar tied the rope made of flowers around the Lord and put the other end of that strong rope around his neck and suffered. In reality, what the Nayanar tied and pulled was a bond of love. It was a rope. As the Nayanar tried to pull the Lord's form with his neck, the Lord, who yielded to the Nayanar's love, would He remain leaning any longer? He would not. The Lord stood straight. The *Shivalingam* stood straight. The Lord stood straight not by the strength of the strong rope that the Nayanar wore externally, but by yielding to the rope of love that he tied within his heart. This is the meaning. If the Lord stood straight by the strength of that strong rope, He should have stood straight when the elephants and soldiers pulled Him before. But the Lord, who did not stand straight then, now yielded to the Nayanar's rope of love, when the Nayanar pulled with a unified mind, and stood straight. This love of the Nayanar is firm love. "Those who desire something will attain it if they are firm in their desire," says Thirukkural. His wife, children, and relatives suffered without food for two days, and he used the *thali* that was meant to buy rice for them to buy *kunguliyam* for the Lord. The firmness of that love is now evident. Seeing the Lord thus stand straight, the Devas rejoiced above. They cheered from the sky and showered flowers. At that time, the armies and soldiers, whose exhaustion the Nayanar tried to share, also rose with great joy. The king folded his hands, worshipped the Nayanar, and bowed at his golden lotus feet, placing them on his head. We will continue to contemplate. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 163, Ilaimalindha Sarukkam, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar Puranam. In Thiruppanandal, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar straightened the leaning *Lingam* of the Lord. Seeing this, the Devas in the sky rejoiced and showered *Karpaga* (wish-fulfilling) flowers. The elephants and armies, who had been exhausted and weakened by trying to straighten the *Shivalingam*, were greatly delighted. Like a withered grove that suddenly flourishes upon receiving rain after a long drought, they rejoiced. The elephants and armies, who had been weakened without straightening the Lord's *Lingam*, now had the opportunity to see the Lord standing straight, which they had longed for. Therefore, they rejoiced. The king praised the Nayanar and fell at his lotus feet, worshipping him. Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar, a devotee, straightened the leaning *Shivalingam*. Sekkizhar Peruman states that straightening the *Shivalingam* of the Lord, who bent the Meru mountain as a bow in the chariot pulled by the Vedas, to burn the three flying cities, can only be achieved by devotees who possess a virtuous love for the Lord's feet. Who can show or witness such special love of devotees? Here, the *Thripura Dhahanam* (burning of the three cities) mentioned by Sekkizhar Peruman has been extensively discussed in the Puranam of Viranmin Nayanar. We have seen how the Lord ascended the Vedic chariot and burned the three cities. We should remember all those events here. Why does Sekkizhar Peruman mention this divine play here? Because Lord Shiva bent the Meru mountain as a bow. Meru mountain is the greatest of all mountains, the king of mountains. Lord Shiva bent such a strong Meru mountain as a bow. That Lord Shiva stood leaning in Thiruppanandal. The *Shivalingam* of Lord Shiva, who bent the mighty Meru as a bow, was leaning. It was the devotee Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar who made that leaning *Shivalingam* stand straight. The mighty Lord, who made the Meru mountain bow, was leaning here. And it was our Nayanar who straightened that leaning Lord. Does this not reveal the Nayanar's love for the Lord's feet? The love that such a Nayanar and other devotees had for the Lord's feet is immeasurable. The Lord's feet, which were unattainable to Thirumal (Vishnu) even after searching to the netherworld, are attained by the love of devotees. Thiruvachagam's *Potri Thiru Agaval* describes this as follows: "The lotus feet, which Brahma and other Devas, led by the four-faced one, worshipped and cried out, and which Thirumal, who pressed down the three worlds with two feet, and the sages of the four directions, with their five senses blossoming, praised, could not be known by the great Thirumal, who became a fierce boar and dug through the seven worlds, and then, exhausted, praised the primal Lord, saying 'Jaya Jaya'." Thus, Lord Shiva was unattainable to the Devas, Thirumal, and Brahma who searched for Him. But He was easily accessible to His devotees. The reason for His accessibility was the unified love that His devotees had for Him. It was the quality of servitude born of that unified love. All inanimate objects here are the Lord's possessions. All other living beings are the Lord's servants. Therefore, the Lord will be accessible to devotees who serve Him, realizing that quality of servitude. All worshipped the *Shivalingam* that now stood straight. The king built a temple there and performed many services in Thiruppanandal. Because the king should have made many entrances in the temple, mandapams, and walls to accommodate the elephants and armies. He should have repaired them. The temple itself should have been repaired to the extent that elephants and armies could pull it together. Now the Lord stood straight. Therefore, the temple had to be restored to its former state. The king did so and repaired the temple. He repaired the sacred garden, sacred pond, and sacred walls. Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar stayed there until the king completed all the services. The king also stayed there and personally supervised and carried out the services of the Shiva temple. It is a rule that devotees who undertake services for Shiva temples should not entrust the work to others and attend to other matters, but should personally supervise the work until it is completed. Here, Sekkizhar Peruman says that the king himself stayed and completed all the services. Thus, after performing all the services and worshipping the *Shivalingam*, the king returned to his capital. Our Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar also praised the Lord's lotus feet, which perform the dance in the hall, and after a few days, returned to Thirukadavur. He continued his services as before in Thirukadavur. During those days, Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, the incomparable leader of Sirkazhi, and Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, the renowned king of *Thandagam* (a type of poetic meter), came together to Thirukadavur. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thirugnanasambandha Peruman here as *Nigaril Kazhi Thalaivar* (incomparable leader of Kazhi). This can be interpreted in two ways: as an incomparable leader, and as a leader who incarnated in the incomparable sacred place of Sirkazhi. The incomparable greatness of Sirkazhi is seen in the Thiruppathigams composed by Thirugnanasambandha Peruman for Sirkazhi. The Thiruppathigams composed by Thirugnanasambandha Peruman for Sirkazhi, such as Thiruviragu, Pal Peyar Pathu, Thiru Ezhukutrirukkai, Thiru Chakkaramattu Eeradi, Thiruviyamagam, etc. Furthermore, Thirugnanasambandha Peruman praises the incomparable greatness of Sirkazhi in his Thevaram as "Peruneriy Piramapuram" (Brahmapuram of the great path), "Narpulavar Tham Pugazh Porpathi" (golden city praised by good poets), "Bodhanai Pon Maraiyor Payilum Pugali" (Pugali where learned Brahmins practice), "Kalaiyin Mevum Manathor Irapporkku Karappilar Poliyum Andhan Pozhil Soozhndha Azhagarum Pugazhi" (beautiful Pugazhi surrounded by groves where those with artistic minds and generous hearts shine), "Poyya Navil Andhanar Vazhum Puravam" (Puravam where truthful Brahmins live), "Kari Thannai Panthori Seithon Pavani Seyyum Pathi" (the city where the elephant-taming one performs His procession), "Kadhalal Saivar Pasupathargal Vanangum Shanbai Nagar" (Shanbai Nagar worshipped by Saivas and Pasupathas with love), "Uravar Kavithai Pulavarkku Oru Nalum Karava Van Kai Kattrvar Serum Kalikkazhi" (Kalikkazhi where learned poets with generous hands gather and never hide their poems), "Kattral Kettal Udaiyargal Vazh Kalikazhi" (Kalikazhi where learned and wise people live), "Vilangal Amar Puyal Marandhu Meen Sanipu Kudhunsalikkum Kalanthanum Kalangalila Peruvan Kaiyudaiya Meyyar Vazh Kazhumalame" (Kazhumalam where true devotees with great generosity live, even when the clouds forget to rain and the fish suffer from drought), and "Thirunthadakkai Muthazhalor Manaigal Thoram Iraivanadhu Thanmai Padi Karunthadang Kannargalal Panthu Ammanai Pattayarum Kazhumalame" (Kazhumalam where dark-eyed women play ball and sing Ammanai songs, praising the Lord's nature in every house of the three-fired Brahmins), and "Parakkum Van Pugazhar Pazhiyavai Parththu Pala Pala Arangalai Payitri Karakkumaru Ariya Vanmaiyal Vazhum Kazhumala Nagar" (Kazhumala Nagar where those with widespread fame, seeing faults, practice various virtues and live with unknown generosity), and "Kalaiyarodu Sruthi Thogai Kattror Migu Kootam Vilaiyayina Settor Tharu Vezhunupuram" (Vezhunupuram where learned scholars and those who have mastered the Vedas gather, and where those who have overcome evil reside). Thirugnanasambandha Peruman has sung about the incomparable greatness of Sirkazhi in his Thevaram hymns. Now, if we take "Nigaril" as an epithet for Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, meaning "incomparable leader," then the incomparable leadership of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman becomes evident to us here. We will discuss this in detail in the verses of the Puranam of Thirugnanasambandha. His leadership is incomparable due to many events in his Puranam, and due to the greatness of being worshipped and praised by Paramacharyas like Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, Aludaiya Nambigal (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal), and religious founders like Shankaracharya. Furthermore, we can see the incomparable leadership of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman through the Lord's gracious act of bestowing liberation upon those who reach Him, and through many other deeds. Now, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thirunavukkarasu Peruman as *Thandaga Chathurar* (master of Thandagam) here. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman is uniquely skilled in *Thiruthandagam*. *Thandagam* is a poetic meter structured with a majority of twenty-six letters, excluding *otru* (consonant dot), forming a type of Tamil musical composition with a specific rhythm. It has two divisions: *Alavazhi Thandagam* and *Alaviyatra Thandagam*. Among the three principal composers of Thevaram, only Thirunavukkarasu Peruman composed Thevaram hymns in this *Thandagam* meter. These *Thiruthandagam* hymns, when recited, melt the flesh and soul of the reciters and excel in inspiring devotion to the Lord. Due to this, Thirunavukkarasu Peruman is given the special title *Thandaga Vendhar* (King of Thandagam). *Chathurar* means one who is skilled or powerful. Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman praises Thirunavukkarasu Peruman as *Thandaga Chathurar*. Furthermore, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Thirunavukkarasu Peruman's fame as *Alar Pugazh* (widespread fame). We will see his fame and his ability to enslave people later in the Puranam of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, the Puranam of Apputhi Nayanar, and in many other places. Sambandha Peruman and Thirunavukkarasu Peruman came together to Thirukadavur. We will see the story of these two great souls worshipping the golden feet that kicked Death, and sitting in Kalayanar's sacred monastery and being worshipped by Kalayanar, in the 247th verse of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman's Puranam and in verses 533 to 536 of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman's Puranam. The second meeting of these two great Paramacharyas took place in Thiruppugalur. From Thiruppugalur, these two traveled together, worshipped the sacred place of Thiruambar, and on their way, came to Thirukadavur and visited the Lord of Thirukadavur. After this, they worshipped in Thiruakkur, Thiru Meeyachur, Thiru Pambaram, and other places, and reached Thiruveezhimizhalai. This is their story. We will discuss all these in detail in their respective Puranams. Thus, as the two Paramacharyas came to Thirukadavur, Kalaya Nayanar, a devotee who had boundless love for them, offered them sacred food in his sacred monastery. When he saw these two great Paramacharyas and great devotees together, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar was filled with unprecedented joy, which surged higher and higher. He was filled with boundless joy, thinking that this was the result and reward of his service of feeding Shiva devotees until now. Because Thirunavukkarasu Peruman and Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, who were filled with immeasurable and boundless love, were enslaved by the Lord due to the abundance of their love. They became Paramacharyas who ruled the world. Therefore, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar rejoiced with great love for them. Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar offered sweet sacred food to devotees and performed *Jangama Puja* (worship of living devotees), and as a result, he also received the rare service of these two great Paramacharyas, worshipped them, and received the Guru's grace. Through this Guru worship, he also received Shiva's grace, which is obtained through *Lingam* worship. Thus, Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar received the blessings of all three types of worship: Guru worship, *Lingam* worship, and *Jangama* worship. Therefore, it is understood that through Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar's *Maheswara Puja*, which was feeding devotees, he received Lord Shiva's grace and the Guru's grace. "If one gives something to the Lord in a temple with a picture, it is for the Lord in the moving temple. If one gives something to the Lord in the moving temple, it is for the Lord in the temple with a picture," says Thirumoola Deva Nayanar's Thirumandiram, isn't it? Thus, when *Maheswara Puja* is performed, it is true that Shiva, the Lord, delights within those devotees and partakes of it. Just as grass and other foods fed to a cow turn into blood, spread throughout its body, and then transform into milk that emerges from its udder, the food offered to devotees transforms into the Lord's grace and manifests in the *Shivalingam*. This is the conclusion of the *Gnana Shastras* (scriptures of wisdom). Therefore, the *Maheswara Puja*, which is feeding devotees, that *Jangama* worship, became the cause of Guru worship and *Lingam* worship, and through it, all three – *Jangama* worship, Guru worship, and *Lingam* worship – were established, and the grace of all three was received. This is what we learn from this. Thus, our Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar lived in Thirukadavur, where Lord Shiva, who punished Manmatha (god of love) with a sugarcane bow and Yama (god of death), is enshrined. As his love grew more and more, and his desire increased, a state of unified mind arose, and he performed many services that came his way. Then he attained *Shiva Padam*, the shade of the Lord's feet. The service performed by Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar was feeding devotees and performing Shiva's services. Kalayanar regularly performed the Shiva service of offering *kunguliyam* incense and the *Maheswara Puja* of offering sweet food to devotees. As his love and desire grew, he performed many other services excellently. Through these services, he attained *Shiva Padam*, the fullness of Shiva's grace. That is, he joined the pervasive power of Shiva's grace. He was freed from the heat of birth and attained the cool shade of the Lord's feet. He attained *Shiva Padam*. That *Shiva Padam* is the *Shiva Sayujya Mukthi* (union with Shiva), the great path from which one does not return to birth. Now, Sekkizhar Peruman says, "Having bowed to Kalaya Nayanar, who possessed the quality and firmness of offering his wife's long *thali* to the Lord and ensuring that the service of *kunguliyam* incense was never interrupted, I will now begin to praise the sacred service of Manakkanjara Nayanar with the help of his grace." Sekkizhar thus concludes the Puranam of Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar and begins the Puranam of Manakkanjara Nayanar. We will continue to contemplate accordingly. "To the devotees of Kalayan, the servant in Kadavur, I am a servant." Praise be to the feet of Kungkuliyakkalaya Nayanar. Praise be to the feet of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. Praise be to the feet of Nambiandar Nambigal. Praise be to the feet of Sekkizhar Peruman. Praise be to the feet of Sivakavimani Ayya, who wrote commentaries on Periya Puranam. Thiruchitrambalam.
